title: Stephen M. Lee, et al. v. Gulf Coast Presbytery
disposition_detail: Specifications 1, 2, and 5 were sustained; specifications 3 and 4 were not sustained. Gulf Coast Presbytery was instructed to re-examine Fell after giving him direct guidance, without any instruction to pass or fail him.
first_summary: The General Assembly partially sustained a complaint challenging Gulf Coast Presbytery’s rejection of Raymond Bradford Fell’s ordination examination on account of his theonomic view. It ordered Presbytery to re-examine Fell after identifying specific biblical and confessional deficiencies, but did not direct the examination’s result. The Assembly urged adherence to its prior statement that no particular view of the judicial law’s present application should define orthodoxy or heresy, and faulted Donald Graham for circulating intemperate materials.
summary: A Session challenged Gulf Coast Presbytery’s refusal to sustain Raymond Bradford Fell’s ordination examination, contending that his theonomic view was improperly treated as disqualifying and that prejudicial materials affected the process. The General Assembly sustained specifications 1, 2, and 5, but not 3 and 4. It ordered re-examination after direct guidance on specific biblical and confessional deficiencies, while expressly refusing to dictate the result. It also urged that no view of the judicial law’s present application should itself define orthodoxy or heresy.

sources.supports: Adoption by the General Assembly, specification-level rulings, re-examination directive, theological qualification, and findings concerning intemperate materials and deficient records.
